observed_composition.finding: 9 of 10 additional queries attempted for this assignment returned results that were either (a) parsed down to only the FIRST WORD of the query — e.g. 'what causes inflation' returned dictionary definitions of the word 'cause'; 'best project management software 2026' and 'best running shoes 2026' returned dictionary definitions of 'best'; 'sign up for spotify premium' returned results about the word 'sign' — or (b) geolocated to the Philippines regardless of query content or explicit US market parameters — e.g. 'plumber near me', 'dentist in austin texas', 'nike air max 270', and 'cheap flights to honolulu' all returned Philippines-based businesses/listings/pricing (.ph domains, PRC/Philippines licensing content, PHP-denominated pricing).

examples.methodology_caveat: This is a genuine, reproducible limitation of this session's fetch infrastructure/tooling — NOT a description of what a real US Google or Bing user sees, and it is NOT reported anywhere in the data.json stats above as if it were a real SERP finding. Recorded here only because the assignment requires saying exactly what was observed and when, and because it is a legitimately useful caution for anyone building 'live SERP checker' tooling the same way: plain HTTP/markdown fetches of Bing are not a reliable proxy for a real, geolocated, JS-rendered browser session, even before considering deliberate bot-mitigation. For these query/intent combinations, the write-up should rely on the aggregate study data in the stats array (Seer Interactive, Whitespark, Ahrefs, Semrush, BrightEdge, Authoritas) rather than a fabricated live screenshot description. Google was separately confirmed fully blocked (interstitial page, see the 'how to tie a tie' example).
